summary: Odius (Ancient Greek: Ὀδίος) is captain of the Halizones from far-off Alybe — "where silver is born" — who leads that contingent with his brother Epistrophus in the Trojan Catalogue. Agamemnon thrusts him from his chariot and kills him with a spear through the breast in Iliad 5. He is distinct from the herald Odius who accompanies the embassy to Achilles.

sections.heading: Halizone captain
paragraphs: Homer's Catalogue places Odius and Epistrophus at the head of the Halizones from Alybe, far from the Paphlagonian coast. Apollodorus' Epitome likewise counts them among the Trojan allies; Strabo discusses Alybe in connection with the Chalybes and related Pontic peoples.
Some notices call them children of Mecisteus. Their role in the poem is that of distant allied captains named in the muster and then drawn into the aristeia of Book 5.

sections.heading: Death
paragraphs: When the gods rouse the battle in Iliad 5, Agamemnon thrusts great Odius from his car and fixes his spear in the captain's back between the shoulders, driving it through the breast until he falls with a thud and his armour clangs.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (odius-halizone) is the Halizone war-leader. Homer also names a herald Odius among those who attend the embassy that tries to persuade Achilles to return to battle (Iliad 9) — a different function and figure sharing the name.
